question: What is the main job of a conceptual framework in a nursing research study?

options.A: To provide a summary of the hospital budget
options.C: To act as a structural map connecting research ideas
options.D: To list the names of all study participants

explanation: Think of a conceptual framework as your research roadmap! It shows how your main ideas and concepts link together to guide your study smoothly. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why do nurse researchers set up a conceptual framework before collecting data?

options.A: To replace the need for a formal literature review
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of conducting the study
options.C: To guarantee that the study gets published immediately
options.D: To make sense of complex human experiences and guide the inquiry

explanation: Research can get messy! A good framework helps you organize your thoughts and makes sure you look at all the important parts of a tricky problem. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h1)

question: What does a conceptual framework mainly display?

options.A: The exact daily schedule of the researcher
options.B: Patient room numbers in a hospital ward
options.C: Key factors and their presumed relationships
options.D: The monetary cost of nursing equipment

explanation: It's like a picture of your thoughts: it shows the main variables you are studying and how you expect them to influence each other. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h2)

question: What happens to a research study if it lacks a clear conceptual framework?

options.A: It stops patients from participating in the project
options.B: It automatically becomes much easier to complete
options.C: It requires fewer ethical approvals from the committee
options.D: It can easily lose focus and gather irrelevant data

explanation: Without a clear map, you might end up collecting tons of information that doesn't actually help answer your research question. Keep it focused! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h2)

question: What is the main difference between a theoretical and a conceptual framework?

options.A: A theoretical framework is based on an established grand theory
options.B: A conceptual framework is never used in nursing research
options.C: A conceptual framework has no variables attached to it
options.D: A theoretical framework is created only by students

explanation: Theoretical frameworks lean on big, already-tested theories (like Nightingale's theory), while conceptual frameworks are often built from scratch for your specific study. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h3)

question: When would a nurse researcher build a conceptual framework instead of using a single theoretical framework?

options.A: When combining ideas from multiple sources to fit a unique study
options.B: When the researcher wants to avoid reading published literature
options.C: When the study has no human participants involved
options.D: When the hospital administration bans the use of theories

explanation: Sometimes one theory isn't enough! When your study has a unique mix of ideas, you blend them together into your own custom conceptual framework. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h3)

question: In a research framework, what is the dependent variable?

options.A: The presumed cause of the health problem
options.B: The outcome or effect being measured
options.C: The abstract mental image with no label
options.D: The personal opinion of the lead nurse

explanation: Remember: the dependent variable is your final result or outcome. It's what changes in response to whatever you are testing! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h4)

question: How does a concept differ from a variable in a research study?

options.A: A concept only appears in the conclusion section
options.B: A variable is never used in quantitative research
options.C: A variable is imaginary, while a concept is physical
options.D: A concept is an abstract idea, while a variable is measured

explanation: A concept is a broad mental thought (like 'pain' or 'anxiety'), but a variable is how you actually measure it in the study (like a pain scale score). [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h4)

question: What is the very first step when you want to develop a conceptual framework?

options.A: Drawing boxes and arrows on a whiteboard
options.C: Reviewing the existing literature on the topic

explanation: You always start by reading what other researchers have already discovered so you know what factors matter most for your topic. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h5)

question: A nurse researcher has finished reviewing literature and picking out variables. What should they do next?

options.A: Destroy all notes taken during the literature search
options.B: Submit the final budget to the finance office
options.C: Select a mapping approach to connect the variables
options.D: Discharge all patients currently in the ward

explanation: Once you have your key variables written down, the fun part starts: figuring out how to draw the lines and boxes to connect them! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h5)

question: How do conceptual frameworks help bedside nurses in everyday clinical practice?

options.A: By helping them understand patient behaviors and treatment responses
options.B: By managing the supply inventory in the treatment room
options.C: By replacing the need to document vital signs in charts
options.D: By calculating the monthly salary of nursing staff

explanation: Frameworks give us a clear lens to understand why our patients react to illnesses and treatments the way they do. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h6)

question: Why is using a shared conceptual framework useful for spreading evidence-based practice?

options.A: It stops nurses from asking questions about new procedures
options.B: It provides a standard language for discussing patient outcomes
options.C: It removes the need for patient consent during studies
options.D: It makes clinical guidelines completely optional for staff

explanation: When all nurses speak the same clinical language, it is much easier to share what works and improve patient care together. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h6)

question: In a study on medication adherence for high blood pressure, what is the most likely dependent variable?
explanation: The dependent variable is your outcome. Here, we want to see if the blood pressure is successfully controlled at the end of the day! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h7)

question: What makes a conceptual framework so useful when you are reading a published nursing study?

options.A: It proves the researcher spent a lot of money on the project
options.B: It lists every single patient who refused to participate
options.C: It makes the study goals and variable relationships instantly clear
options.D: It replaces the abstract and the conclusion sections

explanation: A good diagram or framework gives you a quick snapshot so you can understand the whole study at a single glance. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h7)

question: What is a common trap to avoid when designing a conceptual framework?

options.A: Sharing the research design with student nurses
options.B: Writing the framework on a white sheet of paper
options.C: Making the framework too complex and cluttered
options.D: Using too few words in the title of the study

explanation: Don't try to cram every single idea in the universe into one diagram! Keep it clean, simple, and testable. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h8)

question: How can a nurse researcher make sure their conceptual framework stays practical?

options.A: By avoiding any review of previous literature
options.B: By removing all independent variables from the diagram
options.C: By copying a framework from an unrelated medical study
options.D: By making sure every variable matches a data collection tool

explanation: Every single concept in your framework must be something you can actually measure using surveys, patient charts, or direct observation! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T11#GNS217_U3_T11_h8)
